name: Student Attendance System
tagline: Keep a class roster, mark attendance every school day and flag students below the required percentage.
description: A React and TypeScript web app for recording daily attendance. Teachers add students with roll numbers and classes, mark each student Present, Late or Absent for a date, and see attendance percentages per student and per class. Everything is saved in the browser’s localStorage, so it runs offline with no server or database to set up.
features: Add, edit and delete students with a roll number and class; duplicate roll numbers within a class are rejected.
Mark each student Present, Late or Absent for today or any past date, with a one-click “Mark all present”.
Reopen a saved date to correct attendance, with a warning before unsaved changes are discarded.
Search students by name or roll number and filter attendance records by date range, class, status and student.
Dashboard with today’s status, overall attendance, attendance by class and students below the threshold.
Per-student attendance percentages, counting Late as attended, calculated from the saved records.
Export filtered attendance records as CSV, and export or import a full JSON backup.
Automatic saving to localStorage with validation and safe recovery from corrupted data.
A fictional demo class on first run, plus in-app and manual instructions for resetting data.
limitations: Data is stored in one browser on one device; there is no sync between devices or users.
There are no user accounts or permissions; anyone using the browser can change the data.
Attendance is recorded once per day, not per period or subject.
localStorage holds about 5 MB, which suits a few classes rather than a whole institution.
The interface text is English only; dates and numbers follow the browser’s locale.
learningObjectives: Structure a multi-screen React app with TypeScript types for your data.
Manage state with useReducer and share it through React Context.
Save, load and validate data in localStorage without trusting what is stored.
Write unit and component tests with Vitest and Testing Library.
Build accessible forms, dialogs and status messages.
ideasForExtension: Track attendance per period or subject by storing a period key under each date.
Add a chart of attendance over time for each class.
Replace localStorage with a backend API and database so several teachers can share data.

prerequisites.name: Node.js
prerequisites.note: Node.js 24 LTS is recommended. npm is included.

steps.title: Install the dependencies
steps.note: Needs an internet connection the first time and downloads about 135 MB into node_modules.

steps.title: Start the app
steps.note: Open the address Vite prints, usually http://localhost:5173/. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop.

steps.title: Build for production (optional)
steps.note: Creates an optimised copy in the dist folder and serves it locally.

notes: Attendance data is saved in your browser’s localStorage under the key campuskit-attendance:v1.
To reset data, use Settings in the app, or delete that localStorage entry from your browser’s developer tools.
Change the app name, institution, threshold, accent colour and demo data in src/app.config.json.

covers: Attendance percentages, per-class summaries and date ranges.
Local date handling and impossible dates.
Saving, loading and recovering from corrupted localStorage data.
Student form validation, including duplicate roll numbers and Unicode names.
User flows: adding and editing a student, marking and saving attendance, searching and deleting.

network.notes: npm install downloads packages once. After that the app runs offline and never sends data anywhere.
